parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs national document, federal-facility, entry-fraud and custody exposures with a narrower, unenforced state school/college facility law. A visitor with matching home documents and private services faces mainly friction and age-dependent school/care uncertainty, but discrepancy at entry can lead to refusal, investigation, detention under documented abusive birth-sex/conversion practices, or hormone interruption. Courts have enjoined some measures, hate-crime and employment protections exist nationally, and private/public-accommodation discrimination is barred only in some municipalities. Unremedied universal document/facility rules and severe custody terms place this below the 0.45 profile, while absence of organised police targeting, a criminal bathroom penalty in this state, or a state-wide private-facility ban keeps it above 0.35.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary passport policy stopped new X or non-birth-sex markers in Feb 2025; Supreme Court allowed it Nov 2025. Entry cable directs refusal and more evidence where documents/records create reasonable sex doubt, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful material misrepresentation; passports reportedly blocked/confiscated.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid to expiration. Fraud finding requires four elements, is not automatic, and has limited waivers; passport policy is under civil-liberties litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger refusal, investigation and custody, converting a border issue into detention and birth-sex placement exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 national corrections adopted conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution. Immigration custody reports for trans men include forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse, with guards using gendered justification.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national orders have been blocked or are litigated, but dossier does not document an operative remedy changing the adopted custody practices. Not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry, facility or fraud investigation leading to detention exposes the traveller to the documented custody regime, including medication denial.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities inconsistent with birth sex. This state's 2024/2025 law requires public and private K-12 and colleges to designate bathrooms, locker/changing/shower rooms and overnight accommodation by birth certificate.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-occupancy restrooms are exempt. State law has no criminal penalty or enforcement mechanism and no documented arrest or citation; most non-educational private settings are not covered by this state law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities create nationwide exposure; the state law mainly affects minors, students and overnight educational accommodation rather than ordinary adult visitors.

care_services.exposure: State minor care/sports bill bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery under 18, but was re-enjoined Mar 2025; operative status unresolved. Custody hormone removal is documented. National minor-care executive action and proposed insurance rules are contested.
care_services.protection: Re-enjunction and abandonment of Jan 2024 adult-care proposal mean no documented current adult-care ban. Emergency-care practice for visitors is not documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor needing care, medication continuity or emergency admission faces uncertain state law plus national funding/hostility measures; detention can interrupt hormones.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official measures frame gender identity as ideology, direct school investigations and possible teacher prosecution for facilitating social transition, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender. Polling records 66% support for birth-sex document listing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders are blocked/enjoined and courts remain active; national hate-crime law covers gender identity. Dossier does not document organised police sweeps or extortion in this state.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing increases scrutiny at schools, borders and agencies, while litigation creates variable real-world enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor students must use facilities matching birth certificate, including overnight accommodation. Jan 2025 law requires staff to out LGBTQ students to parents. Care and sports bans are enacted but re-enjoined, status uncertain; national order threatens teachers using preferred names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Single-occupancy exemption and current injunction of care/sports provisions reduce immediate exposure, but guardian rights and school practice are not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor enrolled or housed through an educational institution faces facility, outing and care uncertainty that an adult alone ordinarily does not.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific pattern of street attacks or police targeting of visitors is documented. Public support for birth-sex documents is noted, but underlying incidents and rates are not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate crimes are punishable nationally; state has no gender-identity anti-discrimination statute in private employment, housing or public accommodations, though 33 municipalities have ordinances and a 2018 state executive order covers state employment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Patchy local ordinances and absent state statute make recourse location-dependent if harassment occurs in visitor-facing services.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: July 2026 assessment places state in second-highest tier among 16, based on statutory text/litigation, not measured incidents. Several national and state measures are enjoined or unresolved, including care/sports, adult-care replacement and Aug 2026 vehicle-marker rules.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several orders, ACLU litigation challenges passports, and municipal ordinances provide partial remedies. Other orders remain in effect, including allowed passport restriction.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Traveller cannot reliably assume either full enforcement or full injunction; checking operative status before travel is essential, but uncertainty itself is exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal document/facility exposure, but this case is above 0.35 because the state facility law covers only schools/colleges, has no penalty or enforcement mechanism, and no documented police extortion, raids or state-wide private-facility exclusion. National custody and entry-fraud risks prevent a higher score.

Below 0.45-A: that anchor has an all-public-building birth-sex rule upheld by courts. Here federal facilities plus birth-certificate education rules combine with entry refusal/fraud risk and documented severe custody/medication practices, although the state law itself is narrower and unenforced.

Materially below 0.55-A because exposures are not merely recurring service refusals with some refunds: passport binary policy is court-allowed, discrepancy can support refusal/fraud consequences, federal facilities are restricted, and custody hormone removal and immigration-custody abuse are documented.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document or presentation discrepancy at entry or in a government/educational facility, followed by possible refusal, investigation, detention, birth-sex placement and interruption of hormones. Litigation and local ordinances mitigate some measures, and this state's education law lacks penalties, but they do not cancel the allowed national passport rule, federal facility restriction, uncertain minor-care status, or custody practices. For an adult using private services with consistent documents, daily exposure is substantially lower than the custody/entry worst case; for a minor in education or anyone detained, exposure is much higher.
